newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish stock market strained by new issues.
newsitem.headline: Turkish stock market strained by new issues.

text.p: The level of new Turkish share issues is straining the Istanbul stock market and threatens to drag the market lower, brokers said on Thursday.
They said the share offerings were adding to the negative impact on the bourse of uncertainty in the political arena and concerns about the future of the economy.
"I would say that political uncertainties and new issues drawing money from the market are having a negative influence," said Erhan Topac, general manager at Gedik Securities.

The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,514, down 16 points, or 1.05 percent from Wednesday, but up sligthly from a late low of 1,500. Volume dropped to 17.49 trillion lira ($133.5 million) from Wednesday's 21.12 trillion ($161.5 million).
New issues this year, which have gathered pace in recent weeks, have attracted around six trillion Turkish lira of funds.
But Topac said foreign investors were buying the majority of the new shares.

The market, which gained strongly in the first two months of the year, has been weighed down since by doubts over the future of the Islamist-led coalition in the wake of a military-inspired demand to crack down on a rise in religious activism, brokers said.

"The month of April is generally positive in the market. The first reason for it not being that way this year is the political tensions, the second is that new issues are drawing money from the market," said Alp Tekince, deputy general manager at Bumerang Securities.
Tekstilbank general manager Ertan Gungor shared the view that the current economic environment was not suitable for new issues.

"At this time the bourse cannot cope with this. There is a clear amount of money in the market. The market cannt cope with this at a time of great demand let alone at a time when the market is not active," Gungor said.
